title: South Korea's Cosmax Posts Record Q3 Revenue of 875.8 Billion Won; Operating Profit Jumps 95% - BigGo Finance
text:

 Add preferred source South Korea's Cosmax reported record quarterly results for the third quarter of this year, with consolidated revenue of 875.8 billion won (approximately $656.2 million) and operating profit of 83.3 billion won (approximately $62.4 million). Revenue rose 49.6% from a year earlier, while operating profit surged 94.9%. The South Korean entity led growth with revenue of 616.1 billion won (approximately $461.6 million), surpassing the 600 billion won mark in a quarter for the first time, while overseas units in China (177 billion won), the U.S. (69.5 billion won), Indonesia (28.8 billion won) and Thailand (16.2 billion won) all posted revenue growth. The U.S. unit stayed in the black for a second straight quarter. Cumulative revenue for the first three quarters reached 2.3527 trillion won (approximately $1.8 billion), with operating profit of 210.1 billion won (approximately $157.4 million). Key Elements 
 Cosmax Cosmax Korea Cosmax China Cosmax USA Cosmax Indonesia Cosmax Thailand K-beauty cosmetics ODM South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service Electronic Disclosure System Cosmax (192820), a South Korean cosmetics original design manufacturer (ODM), set a new all-time quarterly record with consolidated revenue of 875.8 billion won (approximately $656.2 million) in the third quarter of this year. Operating profit rose 94.9% from a year earlier to 83.3 billion won (approximately $62.4 million), while net profit surged 317.7% to 44.5 billion won (approximately $33.3 million). Revenue and profit both jumped sharply in the third quarter, which is typically classified as the cosmetics industry's off-season.
 According to a disclosure filed with South Korea's Financial Supervisory Service Electronic Disclosure System on the 11th, revenue increased 49.6% from the year-earlier period. Cumulative revenue for the first three quarters totaled 2.3527 trillion won (approximately $1.8 billion) and operating profit 210.1 billion won (approximately $157.4 million), up 30.9% and 35.6% respectively from a year earlier. "Thanks to the rapid growth of our South Korean entity and the accompanying growth of our overseas units, we set a new quarterly revenue record even in the third quarter, which is the off-season," the company said. "Based on our unrivaled research and development (R&D) and manufacturing capabilities, we will further solidify our position as the world's No. 1 cosmetics ODM."
 The South Korean entity was the engine of growth. Cosmax Korea's third-quarter revenue rose 61% from a year earlier to 616.1 billion won (approximately $461.6 million), and was up 19% from the previous quarter, pushing it above the 600 billion won mark in a quarter for the first time. Operating profit rose 97% to 67.7 billion won (approximately $50.7 million). The result reflects a steady inflow of production orders as major customers expanded online marketing and moved to develop overseas offline distribution channels. In basic skincare, demand for existing products held steady while inquiries for new derma cosmetics products increased, and color cosmetics also posted double-digit growth as new product launches continued. A higher share of production for relatively high-margin items such as essences and mists also helped improve profitability.
 Overseas units all posted revenue growth from a year earlier. The China unit's revenue rose 27% to 177 billion won (approximately $132.6 million). In Shanghai, orders expanded from color cosmetics brands that have built recognition in the local and Asian markets, and basic skincare brands also increased new product launches. In Guangzhou, revenue from major customers grew while the product lineup diversified into sun care and kids' and baby skincare. The U.S. unit grew 88% to 69.5 billion won (approximately $52.1 million). Repeat orders and product-line expansion from existing customers continued, and new development demand emerged across basic skincare categories including creams, essences, masks and sun care. Collaboration with headquarters that shortened product development timelines also had a major effect. The U.S. unit stayed in the black in the third quarter, following its first-ever quarterly profit in the second quarter.
 In Southeast Asia, the Indonesia unit stood out with revenue of 28.8 billion won (approximately $21.6 million), up 34%. A recovery in sales at existing customers and new product launches underpinned results, and growing contacts with customers in neighboring countries such as India and Malaysia are raising the potential for export expansion. The Thailand unit posted revenue of 16.2 billion won (approximately $12.1 million), up 7%. Growth at major customers was supplemented by an influx of new customers from neighboring countries, and development requests increased for basic products such as skincare, sun care and cleansing. Its own brand development and manufacturing (OBM) business, carried out in collaboration with distribution channels, also contributed to revenue.

 Note: Consolidated operating profit is 83.3 billion won (up 94.9%) on a disclosure basis. The South Korean entity's operating profit growth rate is 97%. The U.S. entity recorded operating profit in the third quarter following the second quarter, but the specific amount was not disclosed.
 The results show that expanding K-beauty exports are translating into order growth across the ODM industry. A key factor cited is the continuing trend of small and indie brands without their own production facilities outsourcing manufacturing as they broaden online and overseas distribution channels. With global demand led by skincare holding firm, Cosmax is expanding its order backlog by leveraging the production capacity of its South Korean entity and the local responsiveness of its overseas bases.
 The market is also watching the fourth-quarter earnings trend. The fourth quarter is typically classified as the peak season for the cosmetics industry, as year-end shopping seasons overlap with new product launches. However, how long the U.S. unit's profitability will continue and how closely the China unit's growth rate tracks the pace of local consumption recovery are cited as variables for future results. The expansion of sales networks by Southeast Asian bases such as Indonesia and Thailand into neighboring countries is seen as a medium- to long-term growth driver.
